subject: Data Structures
title: Discover Queues
description: Discover how a Queue stores and removes data.

mission.title: Discover FIFO
mission.description: Find the hidden rule behind a Queue.

discovery.title: First In First Out
discovery.summary: The first item added to a Queue is the first item removed.

sections.title: What is a Queue?
sections.content: A Queue is a linear data structure that keeps items in the order they arrive.

sections.title: FIFO
sections.content: FIFO means First In, First Out: the first item added is the first one removed.

sections.title: Operations
sections.content: ENQUEUE adds an item at the back. DEQUEUE removes an item from the front.

sections.title: Real-world example
sections.content: People waiting in a line are served in the same order that they joined the line.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a waiting line
alternate_explanations.content: A Queue is like people waiting for a bus. New people join at the back, and the person at the front boards first.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through the line
alternate_explanations.content: ENQUEUE A, then B, then C. The line is A → B → C. DEQUEUE removes A first because A has waited the longest.
